subject: Proof of encryption & subprocessor registry for CCPA/CPRA addendum
messages:
From: Marta Reed <marta.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Sato <tom.sato@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: proof of encryption + subprocessor list for CCPA addendum

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the recent call — Acme Health legal needs a couple of specific artifacts so we can sign the CCPA/CPRA service provider addendum. Can you please provide the following by EOD Tuesday (2026-12-22):

- Short (1-2 page) encryption summary describing at-rest and in-transit protections, KMS/HSM usage, key rotation policy, and where keys are stored.
- Current subprocessor registry with regions and date on- boarded.
- Confirmation whether telemetry/operational logs that include customer identifiers are treated as "service provider" data (i.e., not a "sale") under your policies.
- SOC 2 type II date or link and process for audit evidence requests.
- A redline of the Acme Addendum (attached) showing any carve-outs or additional transfer safeguards you need for interstate transfers.

We attached our proposed addendum (AcmeHealth_Addendum_v2.docx) — primary questions are around: (a) whether Redwood will accept a 3rd party subprocessor notice window of 30 days vs 60 days, (b) if Redwood can commit that no offshore subprocessors will process Acme PII without advance notice, and (c) whether telemetry is considered a service provider activity.

Please loop in whoever from security/privacy will be the POC — we want final language before procurement closes this week.

Thanks,
Marta Reed
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Health

Attachments: AcmeHealth_Addendum_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marta Reed <marta.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: proof of encryption + subprocessor list for CCPA addendum

Marta — thanks, got it. Looping in Karthik (sales) and Lauren (privacy/security) to own the artifacts and the redline. Quick response below and we'll follow up with attachments and a redline this afternoon.

At a high level:
- Redwood operates as a CCPA/CPRA Service Provider (we do not "sell" personal information). We can confirm that telemetry/operational logs containing customer identifiers are treated as service-provider data unless specifically scoped out in a customer's contract.
- We use cloud KMS with HSM-backed root keys, TLS 1.2+ for in-transit, AES-256 at-rest. Key rotation cadence: annual for root keys; customer-facing API keys rotated on demand.
- SOC 2 Type II: most recent report is 2026-09; we can provide a redacted copy or sign an NDA to provide full report.
- Subprocessor registry attached; we provide 30-day notice as standard but can offer 60 days for enterprise deals via addendum.

I'll attach: 1) encryption brief, 2) current subprocessor registry, 3) a preliminary redline of your addendum with our preferred language. Lauren will be security POC for any deeper evidence requests.

Docs I will send in follow-up: 20261220-Redwood-Encryption-Overview.pdf; subprocessor_registry_20261220.csv; redline_Addendum_20261220.docx

Next steps: Lauren and I will review the specific clauses you flagged and propose a short set of concessions (if any) plus the DocuSign-ready addendum by EOD. If Acme wants an on-site or live security review, let's schedule early next week.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: 20261220-Redwood-Encryption-Overview.pdf (application/pdf), subprocessor_registry_20261220.csv (text/csv)

From: Marta Reed <marta.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Sato <tom.sato@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 12:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: proof of encryption + subprocessor list for CCPA addendum

Thanks Rishi — quick clarifications:

1) Telemetry: if logs contain patient identifiers (PHI that is also personal information), Acme treats that as restricted and needs an explicit handling clause. Can you confirm whether logs with identifiers are purged automatically and the retention period?
2) Subprocessors: curious which subprocessors handle model hosting vs telemetry/logs vs payments. Can you add a column in the registry that lists "purpose"?
3) Redline: we'll review your preliminary redline but can you highlight any clauses you consider non-negotiable (e.g., audit notice windows >30 days, offshore subprocessors)?

Also attaching our redline of sections 2 and 5 that matter most to Procurement. If you can return a DocuSign link with your addendum by EOD Tuesday we can move forward.

Thanks,
Marta

Attachments: Acme_Addendum_sections_2_5_upd.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed addendum language + negotiation points (Acme)

Rishi / Lauren — drafting notes for the Acme deal (ACME-2026-REW-77):

- Offered concessions: 60-day subprocessor notice (we'll commit to 60 days for Acme), redacted SOC2 on NDA, and a signed addendum that includes a data flow diagram for Acme's account.
- Non-negotiables we should flag in a redline: unlimited audit rights are not acceptable; we propose scoped audit (one annual) with reasonable notice and audit scope defined. We also cannot commit to an absolute offshore ban; we can commit to advance notice plus a remediation path and the ability to object for critical subprocessors.
- Telemetry: propose language that telemetry/operational logs are considered service-provider data for product telemetry; any PHI-specific telemetry will be handled under the encountered data clause and subject to retention limits (default 90 days) unless a different SLA is negotiated.
- Timeline: I recommend returning a DocuSign-ready addendum by EOD Tuesday to meet Acme procurement.

I'll add these as tracked changes to the redline_Addendum_20261220.docx and circulate. Lauren — can you confirm the 90-day default on logs and whether we can shorten to 30 days for PHI-related fields?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_Addendum_20261220.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marta Reed <marta.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: proof of encryption + subprocessor list for CCPA addendum

Marta — attaching the items we discussed and next steps.

Summary attached: 20261220-Redwood-Encryption-Overview.pdf (high-level, 2 pages)
Registry attached: subprocessor_registry_20261220.csv — includes "purpose" column separated into hosting / telemetry / payments / analytics.
Redline attached: redline_Addendum_20261220.docx — includes Karthik's suggested concessions and the language we discussed re: telemetry retention (default 90 days, can shorten to 30 days for PHI fields with customer configuration).

We can accept: 60-day subprocessor notice for this enterprise contract; advance notice + right to object for offshore subprocessors; scoped audit (annual, narrow scope) with NDA and redacted findings for public release.

Links: DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/exec/ABC123
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/ACME-77
Drive folder (artifacts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example

Lauren is the security POC for any evidence requests — lauren_bishop@redwood.com. If Acme confirms acceptance of the redline, Karthik will push DocuSign and we aim to close before EOW.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
